provenance.pins: two-terminal BIDIRECTIONAL TVS in SMC(DO-214AB); pin numbers A1/A2 from the EasyEDA Pro symbol via tools/eda.py. No cathode band and no polarity. vMax is Vrwm = 40 V, the continuous limit - NOT the 64.5 V clamping voltage, which is what the part produces at its own 23.3 A rated surge.

designVerdict: SELECTED as D7, D8, D9 - the bus TVS. One across VBUS to GND and one across each channel output to LED_RTN.
notes: SMCJ40CA, bidirectional, SMC(DO-214AB). Vrwm 40 V, Vbr 44.4-49.1 V, Vc 64.5 V at Ipp 23.3 A, 1.5 kW at 10/1000 us.

CHOSEN ON STANDOFF, NOT ON HEADLINE CLAMP. A 36 V part (SMAJ36CA, C19077551) sits UNDER the 37.8 V a compliant fixed PDO may hold indefinitely, where leakage is unspecified and strongly temperature-dependent. 40 V is the next standoff rung - the ladder has nothing between 36.8 and 40 V - so it is the lowest that clears the bus.

THE HEADLINE CLAMP COMPARISON IS INVALID and it is how this choice was first got wrong. 64.5 V here against the SMA part's 58.1 V compares two DIFFERENT currents: each Vc is quoted at that part's own rated surge, 23.3 A for a 1.5 kW SMC against 6.9 A for a 400 W SMA. Work the dynamic resistance R_d = (Vc - Vbr)/Ipp instead: 0.66 Ohm here against 2.01 Ohm, so this part clamps to 55.7 V at 10 A where the SMA part reaches 64.3 V, crosses the 60 V TPS54360B and SS36 rating at 16.5 A against 7.8 A, and the eFuse's 67 V at 27.1 A against 11.3 A.

ORDERING AGAINST THE eFUSE OVP: Vbr 44.4-49.1 V sits entirely ABOVE the TPS16630's 39.1-42.3 V OVP window with 1% resistors, so the eFuse always sheds the load before this part starts dissipating. The retired 36 V part's 40.0-44.2 V overlapped that window and the order depended on corners. The cost is a 2.1 V band, 42.3 to 44.4 V, where neither acts.

J1 IS NOT PROTECTED AND CANNOT BE. The CX90B-16P is rated 48 V AC/DC and this part does not conduct until 44.4 V at its low breakdown corner, and reaches 48 V there at 5.4 A - while at the high corner (49.1 V) it never conducts below the connector's rating at all. The 1.9 A figure belongs to the retired SMA part, whose 2.01 Ohm R_d is three times this one's. No 37.8 V-standoff avalanche TVS can protect a 48 V connector: its breakdown must sit above the bus, which is already near the connector's rating. Recorded as the residual in the design README.

vMax in the pin map is Vrwm (40 V), NOT the 64.5 V clamping voltage. Vc is what the part PRODUCES during a surge; recording it as a limit tells the ERC the part is happy at 64 V, which is how three records here were wrong before.
